system.name: vLLM / PagedAttention
system.one_liner: an LLM serving system that manages KV cache memory in fixed-size, non-contiguous blocks, inspired by OS virtual memory paging

content.subject: how one query token's key/value vectors are spread across three fixed-size blocks stored non-contiguously in physical memory

content.key_idea: One request's key/value vectors are split into fixed-size blocks (4 tokens each) that PagedAttention stores in whatever physical block-table slots are free, so logically adjacent blocks need not be physically contiguous.
content.reading_order: left to right from the green query-vector box, following the three arrows to Block 1, Block 2 and Block 0 in the physical block table, then within each highlighted row left to right through its word cells

The key and value vectors are spread across three blocks, and the three blocks are not contiguous

summary: Figure 5 illustrates PagedAttention's core memory layout with one concrete example. A query vector for the token 'forth' (green box) fans out to three blocks of a physical key/value block table, each block holding up to four tokens' key/value vectors: Block 1 holds 'years, ago, our, fathers', Block 2 holds only 'brought, forth' so far (two slots still free), and Block 0 holds 'Four, score, and, seven', the start of the Gettysburg Address opening line. Blank white rows sit between the three highlighted blocks in the table, representing other physical blocks unrelated to this sequence. Because logical Block 0, Block 1 and Block 2 are drawn in non-adjacent physical rows, the figure visually demonstrates the paper's central claim: unlike a normal KV cache, PagedAttention lets a request's key/value blocks live in non-contiguous physical memory, closing the gap that fragmentation used to waste.
